chapter: Trumpet teachers and St. Louis heroes
title: Bandmaster Richardson and the St. Louis trumpet studio
summary: Besides bandmaster Richardson, Thomas studied weekly with St. Louis Symphony trumpeters Gustadt, Carrionie and Olivieri at $3.50 per half hour.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: were musical. Mr. Richardson, the bandmaster ...
That was the name you couldn't think of before?

Yeah, I could think of his name. He played trumpet. He wasn't a tremendous trumpet player but he was a tremendous teacher. And during the course of that time they had a trumpet studio in St. Louis. So, I left Mr. Langford and moved up to Jeff City now. And I'm talking to a few people, I heard about this trumpet studio there. And, there was Mr. Gustadt (?) the first trumpeter of our symphony, St. Louis Symphony ...
Who?
Mr. Gustadt, Joe Goostat.
How do you spell that?
I think it's G-u-s-t-d-a-t-d. (sic).
No, I think Clark Terry Gustadt mentioned Gustaff I think it was.
No, it's Gustadt.
Oh, well, we spelled it wrong then.
It's Gustadt. And they had three trumpet players, three trumpet pieces there -- Mr. Gustadt and Mr. Davioni.
How do you spell that?
I think C-a-r-r-i-o-n-i-e and Mr. Antaine(?) Oliveri and please, get that name right.
JTHOMAS (1)
Antoine?
Well, how do we spell it?
Let's see. That's going to be ... 0-l-i-v-i-e-r-i.
Now where are these cats? Are they all in the St. Louis Symphony?

Mr. Gustadt was a first trumpet player in the St. Louis Symphony. Mr. Carrionie was a second trumpet player in the St. Louis Symphony. Mr. Olivieri was a tremendous teacher. He did some things around town with the symphony, substitute things and that kind of thing. I felt one of the greatest teachers I ever met between him and Mr. Langford, you know.
That was a real place for trumpet teachers.
Yeah, but dig this. It cost $3.50 for one-half hour.
Three dollars?
And 50 cents for one-half hour.
WOW.
You'd better believe it.
Now when did you go to this trumpet studio?
Let me see. What about ...
Would it be about your third year at Jeff City?
Yeah, you're quite right, somewhere in there.
You'd go to them during the summer?
Yeah.
And, how often did you do that?
JTHOMAS (1) 44
Every week.
You did?
I had to. I was interested inneent.
That was very good, though, wasn't it?
Well, I guess.
They did a lot for you, I take it.
I think so. Mr. Gustadt was a tremendous soloist (?).
